reviews.text: Beautiful, well maintained campground. Very clean. Although busy, was quiet at night when we were there on a weekend in June. Warm water showers and an outdoor sink for washing dishes. Hikes are amazing.
reviews.title: (无标题, 2026年6月)

reviews.text: A friend and I visited Manning Park for three days in August 2020. We stayed at the Lightning Lake campground, but had to switch sites after the first night (I could not reserve two consecutive nights at any site in the park). This was not a problem, as it seems that every site has the same amenities, and all offer a degree of privacy/separation from neighbouring sites. We had no trouble fitting our gear into the available space, and the ground was level (although covered in large pebbles - bring a cot or a camp pad to sleep on). This campground has designated quiet hours (10 pm - 8 am, I think), and people seemed to be pretty good about respecting them. Park rangers drove around the grounds frequently, offering firewood for sale ($8), and telling people about the nightly presentations at the amphitheatre. There were tons of kids around, riding their bikes and enjoying the playground. The daily temperatures were good, but it did get quite cold overnight (about 4 C), which was what the weather forecast had predicted. We thoroughly enjoyed the campground, and look forward to coming back next season.
reviews.title: Excellent campsites, convenient facilites, beautiful setting

reviews.author: reddefinition
reviews.text: It's a 2-3 hour drive away from Vancouver. Lots of fun activities for everybody - canoeing, kayaking, paddle boarding, swimming, trekking. Too bad you can only park 1 car in campsite for free. need to pay $12 for an extra car overnight. Swimming area is okay, a bit cold for the summertime. There are activities/events posted on their website and around the camping area so watch out for those. we were there for the lantern lights festival and it was awesome. road is a bit dusty especially if there are drivers who doesn't follow the 15KPH speed limit but rangers are doing something about it. be careful on making a wrong turn when looking for your campsite when you arrive. gas is available 20km away. they next one is in Hope, BC - so gas up before going here. They do have gas containers in the resort though, 4KM away from camp grounds. No telco signal here. Wifi available in the resort. there is a great viewpoint on the other side of the resort - scary drive up the hill. boat launch is far if you decide to walk it from camp site. 40 minutes for slow walkers. all in all, still a fun place to camp! good option near vancouver!
reviews.title: Not impressed

reviews.author: WNickel
reviews.text: Lovely campground with large sites. This campground is part of the BC provincial park system and can be booked through their website. Lots of trees give shade and privacy. The lake is for non-motorized boats and a awesome place to kayak or paddle board. There is a boat rental place which is open part of the year, so check ahead if you are going off season. The lake is a short 5 minute walk from the campground and has many things to do. Boat, fish, or swim in the crystal clear water or take a walk around the lake on the forest trail. Park rangers hold different information seminars each day in summer to learn about the surrounding area. Bathrooms are clean with flush toilets (not pit toilets). Kids playground as well makes this a great campground. Take a drive up to the alpine meadows for more hiking or challenge yourself with a climb to the peak of one of the surrounding mountains. When you get tired of cooking head to the lodge restaurant which is a short 7 min drive away. The lodge has a small store for those things you may have forgotten to bring. Beautiful mountain setting...Enjoy.
reviews.title: Great camping option in BC

reviews.author: caroline v (Bruinisse, Netherlands)
reviews.text: We started off our 3 week RV tour in BC on Lightning Lake Campground. What a great way to start! Beautifully located, spacious campsites and well maintained washrooms and showers. Can recommend this park to anyone.
reviews.title: (caroline v, 2019年10月)

reviews.author: Dianne B (White Rock, Canada)
reviews.text: Spaces were far apart allowing for some privacy. A very large camp site that was full on the weekend. The hiking around Lightening, Flash and Strike lakes was excellent. Trail in good condition. Undulating not too steep in any spots. Need to watch footing - lots of exposed roots. Kid and pet friendly.
reviews.title: (Dianne B, 2019年6月)

reviews.author: jan k (Dublin, Ireland)
reviews.text: Everything was very close, even the washrooms, showers and the beach. They even had an area for washing up dishes and a playground for kids. The sites were pretty private because of thick, tall trees between them. It's a busy campground, though.
reviews.title: Busy campground

reviews.author: rhinoab (Hong Kong, China)
reviews.text: This campsite has various plots well spaced with trees to make it your private space and a picnic bench and firepit. Fine for large RVs. The staff were very attentive and you could buy firewood and a starter from them at the gatehouse of as they drove around. This is obviously a favourite place with local families as the roads were full of children on their bikes (safe to do so). The park was clean, showers were well maintained and bins were never full. The beautiful lightning lake is the highlight with 4 or 8 km trail around it, as well as the entertainment of the ground squirrels, think Canadian meerkats, and boat rental to float away an hour or two. Get in the groove and spend at least 2 days.
reviews.title: Great provincial camping ground

reviews.author: nathalielouis87 (Leuven, Belgium)
reviews.text: Stayed here at beginning of our holiday and at the end. Really loved it. Campground is big, clean and friendly staff. Showers and toilets where new and very clean. Environment is beautiful!! A lot of hikes to explore.
reviews.title: (nathalielouis87, 2017年9月)

reviews.source: TripAdvisor (E.C Manning Provincial Park 景点页)
reviews.text: Manning Park is HUGE. It's a very big park with a number of different access points, camp grounds, etc. We booked a campsite at the Lightning Lake campsite and there was a number sites at this particular location. It was walking distance to Lightning lake which isn't a huge lake but for the most part, it was not a busy lake. There are 2 main bathroom/washroom hubs on the site and surprisingly, there was hardly ever a wait for the showers. Great hot water with excellent water pressure. Facilities were well maintained, compared to other sites we have been to so it was a bonus. There are water taps peppered througout the grounds so you don't have to walk far for water. Not all the sites have 'great' separation between sites but the one that we got, luckily, had at least a nice 15ft gap between the sites from each side of us. There is a fire pit and picnic bench on each site but during the fire ban, only portable fire pits are allowed so come with that if you want to stay warm. Overall, it was a nice campground for a 3night family camp out. BUT that said, it is not a site that had any particular 'wow' factor that made it unique. Not sure if we would come back to this site but it was a nice campground to check out.
reviews.title: camping at lightning lake

reviews.author: Susie C (Vancouver, Canada)
reviews.source: TripAdvisor (E.C Manning Provincial Park 景点页)
reviews.text: The spots are nicely spaced out so that you have some privacy. The washrooms are very clean and the showers warm! There are beautiful trails for easy hikes! There was a black bear sighting in the campground during dinner in the evening, and the attendants were there to keep everyone calm and ensure we stay safe as it left the grounds. We woke up to bear poop outside our tent in the morning. Exciting! Ha ha. $33/night for tent camping, and $8/bundle of wood. No cell reception anywhere near the park. On the highway there is a lodge with a payphone, as well as groceries, beer, supplies (hot coffee in the morning!)
reviews.title: (Susie C, 2015年9月)

reviews.author: sueQ5133PX (Vancouver, Canada)
reviews.source: TripAdvisor (E.C Manning Provincial Park 景点页)
reviews.text: There are quite a few different camping spots in the park, but next time I would definately stay at one further away from the highway, maybe around Lightning Lake as the noise from trucks zooming by was significant. A beautiful area though with something for everyone such as short and more difficult hikes and canoes, kayaks and paddle boards for hire at Lightning Lake. Lots of Wildlife too. Would definately go back.
reviews.title: (sueQ5133PX, 2015年8月)

reviews.source: TripAdvisor (E.C Manning Provincial Park 景点页)
reviews.text: We just returned from another late-July trip to Manning Provincial Park, and once again, our trip included a 4-night stay in a cabin at the Manning Park Resort. Like last year, walking portions of some of the easy to access and walk forested trails within the Park, occupied our early-morning hours each day. Our walks took place basically on the same trails as last year (along the Similkameen River near our lodging, Beaver Pond Trail, Canyon Nature Trail, Rein Orchid Trail, Trail to Spruce Bay Beach, and Lightning Lake), plus, a portion of the downstream end of Lightning Lake, which we discovered for the first time this year. Thankfully, we did not have any big animal encounters (like bear, cougar, or the like), but we did get to enjoy some sightings of mule deer (adult, and young-of-the-year), marmots, ground squirrels, a skunk, rabbits/hares, many species of birds (especially enjoyed the encounters with loons, and ravens), and the many varieties of flora at each. Once again, the natural sights and sounds of what we experienced during our stay in Manning Park sure worked their magic on us. And with the clear, bright blue skies, and fresh, clean air during our stay, it shined in all its glory!
reviews.title: Lightning Lake camping

reviews.source: TripAdvisor (E.C Manning Provincial Park 景点页)
reviews.text: We returned recently from another summer visit to E.C. Manning Provincial Park. For us, another mid-July stay, and as done during past visits, we lodged (for our 4-night stay) in a cabin at the Manning Park Resort. Our trail walks, as before, were on several easily-accessible, and very walkable trails. Lightning Lake Day Use Area: familiar activities confined to area adjacent Lake. Lovely, scenic views, especially quiet and beautiful in the early-morning hours. Shared several of the quiet morning moments with some local fauna (marmots, various species of birds, two deer during one visit, and many trout 'jumping'). Many photos were posted on previous trips. Lightning Lake Trail - around 'Lone Duck Bay': trail winds around south and north sides of this small Bay off the main Lake - south side trail nicely-groomed, somewhat elevated from the Lake, and provided spectacular sights & sounds of the Lake, and surrounding forest. We walked portions of this trail on three early-mornings of our stay, and literally revelled in the natural beauty of the area!! Once again, we were able to experience some of Manning Park's splendor and natural beauty, for some up-close, and much-enjoyed personal views. And all accompanied by that clean & fresh, mountain, and forest air!!
reviews.title: Great for camping
